task.description: Run the project's full regression test gate (mix letflow.check.test, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted) and report real pass/fail results before RELEASE-VALIDATOR's independent re-verification.

result.note: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean, zero output/warnings. `mix format --check-formatted` -> clean, exit 0. `mix letflow.check.test` (full partitioned suite): first attempt at N=nproc=8 hit ISS-0219 (documented in README.md's test_parallel.sh section) -- Postgres too_many_connections FATAL 53300 errors cascaded across partitions 4/5/7 (10 failures total: Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest's isolated lua_wallclock_race sub-mix-test, Letflow.ServiceCatalogReaperTest x3 concurrent-guard tests, Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest x3 concurrent-guard tests, Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest x2 rust-pin tests) -- this is the exact known 8-core-host connection-budget artifact README.md documents ('4 is known-good on at least one dev host'), NOT the tenant_template stale-cache signature (no clone_failed / relation-does-not-exist-mentioning-tenant_template errors appeared anywhere in any partition log -- confirmed by grep across all 8 partition logs), so no ORCH escalation needed for that hazard. Re-ran with TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 per README's documented mitigation: reduced from 10 failures to 3. Combined totals across the 4 partitions of this run: 3357 passed, 3 failed, 22 excluded (3382 total examples: partition-1 913 passed; partition-2 826 passed/1 excluded; partition-3 759 passed/1 excluded; partition-4 859/862 passed/20 excluded, 3 failed). The remaining 3 failures, individually diagnosed: (1) 'ISS-0426: :lua_wallclock_race tag-partition integrity' (test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs:1467) -- this test itself shells out to a nested isolated `mix test --only lua_wallclock_race` subprocess needing its own DB pool; at N=4 the concurrent peak from 4 sibling partitions plus this nested subprocess's own pool still transiently exceeded the same Postgres too_many_connections ceiling (FATAL 53300, identical error class to the N=8 run, just far less frequent). Independently re-ran this exact test file/tag alone, uncontended: `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs --only lua_wallclock_race` -> 'Result: 11 passed, 45 excluded', 0 failures -- confirms this is the same local connection-budget artifact, not a code regression, and not the tenant_template hazard either. (2)+(3) 'rust pin (REQ-165) a matching/mismatched rust pin reports OK/MISMATCH' (test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:274,289) -- both fail with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)`; confirmed via `which rustc` / `rustc --version` that this host has no Rust toolchain installed at all -- an environment/toolchain gap (no Rust, only Elixir/Erlang present), unrelated to REQ-229's diff (neither failing test file is touched by this branch's changes: `git diff --stat 9613d348..HEAD` only touches lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex, test/letflow/entities/record/projector_test.exs, and design/handoff docs). None of the 3 residual failures are attributable to REQ-229's changes; all 3 are pre-existing local-sandbox environment limitations (connection budget at concurrency peak, missing rustc). Recommend TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 (or lower) as this host's working value, and flagging the rustc-toolchain gap separately if REQ-165's check-toolchain tests need to be exercised reliably on this host. Directly relevant to REQ-229: independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/entities/record/projector_test.exs` alone (fresh, this run) -> 'Result: 10 passed', 0 failures, matching REVIEWER's step-02d figure exactly; no failure entry for Letflow.Entities.Record.ProjectorTest anywhere in any of the 4 partition-4 (N=4) logs either.
